segmentation.text: A driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise due care
to avoid a collision with a pedestrian.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, the definition that applies: 'every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails', which 'does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; the run's reading classifies the classes under that id, so the aggregate is claimed whole and never expanded into class atoms. 'A driver of' names who controls the vehicle, no class: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing, observable_reading agency).

'a collision' is rel.contact: 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'. Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss' does not apply: the collision itself is what the duty is to avoid, and the approach short of contact is read by the operationalization of 'due care', not by this atom. 'a pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian: 'a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'; claimed whole and read for every road user of the scene other than ego.

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: while the motor vehicle moves (drv.motion.at_rest under p.rest_speed_tolerance does not hold), a pedestrian whose centre it approaches within the time-to-collision horizon p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance) is a conflict the driver's care did not avoid; the projected distance enters the bound itself, so a nearer approach is a graver one. Care is a state of mind and the standard is the whole duty: the rule is a surrogate.

applicability: ego is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle). The duty is judged at every observation.
obligation: At every observation, for every road user p of the scene other than ego that is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): either ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest with p.rest_speed_tolerance), or ego and p are not in contact (rel.contact) and it is not the case that their centres approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) with a centre distance at that closest approach below p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). With no pedestrian in the scene the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'due care' is read only as the avoidance of contact and of a projected close approach to a pedestrian while the vehicle moves; lookout, warning and attention are read only through that outcome, and contact made while the vehicle is at rest is not read as a want of care.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: ego, a passenger car (ru.motor_vehicle), drives along a roadway toward a pedestrian crossing in front of it; the centres are projected to approach within the horizon to a distance below the pedestrian clearance, and ego keeps moving.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: ego drives past a pedestrian walking on the sidewalk well clear of the roadway; no projected approach falls below the clearance within the horizon and there is no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: ego is a bicycle (ru.bicycle), which the motor vehicle aggregate does not include; it rides close past a pedestrian.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: as in permit, the projected approach stays above the clearance, but the source does not observe contact between bodies, so whether ego touches the pedestrian it passes is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: ego drives along an empty road with no pedestrian anywhere in the scene: the duty binds ego alone and is met.

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
may proceed
with due care
on the immediately adjacent highway
to move around such an obstruction.
Such a pedestrian:
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
as possible;
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and
(d) Must return to the sidewalk
as soon as practicable.

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian: 'a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'; claimed whole.

st.sidewalk is the 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', which carries DEF-NRS-484A-240 ('that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians'); ego's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies) is its walking on it, read at the earlier observation at which ego met the obstruction. 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk' does not apply: no crossing is read.

st.obstruction is 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user', kinds including sidewalk_fixture, barrier, excavation, debris: an object in the pedestrian's way on the sidewalk. 'encounters' is ego at the obstruction while on the sidewalk: drv.position.near_region(ego, o) with the reach p.obstruction_reach, over the body-to-region distance of st.region_geometry, the anchor of the obstruction to ego. 'to his or her mobility' is read through ego's conduct at it (s8): it leaves the sidewalk there.

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap on s4): a short section of the sidewalk that is missing is no 'physical object' (st.obstruction), and the absence of a sidewalk region (st.sidewalk) is not a stretch a source records that a pedestrian meets. The example widens where the permission and the duties arise; dropping it would leave the rule unapplied where the law applies.

'may proceed' is ego's travel off the sidewalk on the travelled part of the way, the conduct the care qualifies: its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a region of kind st.travel_region, the abstract union of 'a lane ..., a bicycle lane or path, a roadway ..., a shoulder, or an intersection', which excludes 'a sidewalk'; it proceeds where it is not at rest (drv.motion.at_rest).

'the immediately adjacent highway' is the same way as the sidewalk: the travel region ego occupies and the sidewalk it left both lie on one highway region (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: nearness to a way' is respected: belonging is read through st.on_way, never a distance.

'to move around such an obstruction' is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading purpose): since the last observation at which ego occupied the sidewalk while at that obstruction (drv.position.near_region), ego has occupied no sidewalk. 'such an obstruction' is the one s3 binds, re-bound with the same relations.
'Such a pedestrian' is the pedestrian of s1 who proceeds on the highway under the first sentence: the same binder, the same admitted aggregate.

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: while the pedestrian moves on the highway (drv.motion.at_rest under p.rest_speed_tolerance does not hold), a road user that is not a pedestrian (ru.pedestrian does not hold) whose centre it approaches within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance) is a conflict the pedestrian's care did not avoid; the projected distance enters the bound. Care is a state of mind: the rule is a surrogate.

residues.why: A permission to walk in either direction on the highway: no duty of this node turns on the direction of travel, so the duty is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is a pedestrian. At the judged observation ego occupies no sidewalk and occupies a travel region x (st.travel_region) lying on a highway h (st.on_way) on which a sidewalk s also lies; and, since the last observation at which ego occupied s while at an obstruction o (drv.position.near_region with p.obstruction_reach), ego has occupied no sidewalk at any observation (a since operator). The case of a missing section of sidewalk is not carried (gap on s4).
obligation: At the judged observation: ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest with p.rest_speed_tolerance), or for every road user u other than ego that is not a pedestrian (ru.pedestrian), it is not the case that their centres approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) with a centre distance at that closest approach below p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). With no such road user in the scene the duty is met.

narrowings.why: The purpose of moving around the obstruction is read through the conduct it explains: the pedestrian left the sidewalk at the obstruction and has not yet returned.
'due care' is read only as the avoidance of a projected close approach to a road user other than a pedestrian while the pedestrian moves on the highway.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
A person driving a motorcycle, moped
or trimobile
or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow
if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection;
(2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change
because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter;
(3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn,
if applicable;
and
(4) The person yields the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}' and 'several states may be displayed at once': a steady red with a green turn arrow is circular_red displayed together with green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn); 'steady' excludes flashing_red, 'turn' excludes green_arrow(straight). Read at ego's entry into the intersection, the event the words fix it to.

'motorcycle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels'); 'moped' as DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped ('a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle that is propelled by a small engine'); each claimed whole. 'A person driving' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Nearest atom only, to show the shortfall (gap on b3): no definition applies to 'trimobile', and ru.motorcycle ('motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants') leaves out a three-wheeler seated in a cabin or side by side, which the word admits; ru.motor_vehicle would admit every car.

'bicycle' admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycle' as DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts'), 'electric scooter' as DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor'); each claimed whole.

'facing the signal': the signal controls the approach ego enters through. dev.governs is 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'; the approach is a carrier ego occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that intersection'); its kind is st.travel_region. No halt place is read from dev.governs ('Not a stand-in for: a position').

'proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow' is the movement ego makes through the intersection (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; entered and left through rel.occupies): its heading change since entering it (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, which takes the intersection as its region formal) read at the exit, lying in the straight band (neither turn band) or in the turn band opposite a displayed green arrow (dev.traffic_signal green_arrow(dir)): the right band under a left arrow, the left band under a right arrow.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) [NRS-484B-307-9b],
vehicular traffic
facing the signal
may enter the intersection
only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}' and 'several states may be displayed at once': a steady red with a green turn arrow is circular_red displayed together with green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn); 'steady' excludes flashing_red and 'turn' excludes green_arrow(straight). Read at ego's entry into the intersection, the event the words fix it to.

'traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'. The law's own qualifier 'vehicular' limits the members the duty reads and leaves out pedestrians (and ridden or herded animals, which no class atom carries): carried beside the aggregate as the condition that ego is not ru.pedestrian ('a person on foot, in a wheelchair, or on a device the jurisdiction treats as on foot'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a person on a bicycle or scooter' is why riders of bicycles and scooters remain vehicular traffic, as paragraph (b) confirms by excepting them.

'facing the signal': the signal controls the approach ego enters through. dev.governs is 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'; the approach is a carrier ego occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that intersection'); its kind is st.travel_region, which dev.governs and st.lane_enters range over. No halt place is read ('Not a stand-in for: a position').

'enter the intersection' is the observation at which ego's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies) the intersection (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', which carries DEF-NRS-484A-105's 'area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines' and its exclusion of an alley junction), the region the words single out.

'the movement indicated by the green turn arrow' is the turn whose direction the displayed arrow names (dev.traffic_signal green_arrow(dir)); the movement ego makes is its heading change since entering the intersection (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, which takes the intersection as its region formal), read at the exit and bounded by the reading's turn bands: the left band for a left arrow, the right band for a right arrow, the reversal band for a U-turn arrow.

residues.why: An advisory to drivers turning with the arrow about the signal opposing traffic faces: it imposes no duty and states no condition of this one, so the duty is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) and not a pedestrian (ru.pedestrian). The judged observation is one at which ego leaves an intersection I (ego occupies I at the observation before and not at the judged one), whose last entry (the rise of ego's occupancy of I with no later rise, read through a since operator) took place while ego occupied a carrier c of kind st.travel_region entering I (st.lane_enters(c, I)) and a traffic signal d governing c or I (dev.governs) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn) at that entry observation. Exception: not where any node of paragraph (b) applies to ego (ruleApplies NRS_484B_307_9b_o1 to _o4, ego to ego; they share one applicability).
obligation: For the intersection I and signal d selected as in the applicability (re-bound with the same relations): ego's heading change since its entry into I (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(ego, I) with p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph), read at the judged exit, lies in the band of a green turn arrow d displayed at that entry: at or above p.left_turn_min_angle and at or below p.left_turn_max_angle where green_arrow(left) was displayed; at or below the negative of p.right_turn_min_angle and at or above the negative of p.right_turn_max_angle where green_arrow(right) was displayed; with magnitude at or above p.u_turn_min_angle and at or below p.u_turn_max_angle where green_arrow(u_turn) was displayed. A heading change in none of the displayed arrows' bands (straight through, or a turn against the arrow) violates the duty.

narrowings.why: The movement is read as the heading change through the intersection, from the entry to the exit, against the turn bands of the reading; a movement whose heading change lies in a displayed arrow's band is that arrow's movement whatever lane it ends in.

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during
not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: A signal 'of intention' is the signal itself: sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}', or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}', on the side of the turn ('to turn right or left, or otherwise turn ... from a direct course'), the turn itself being read by t8's concepts. 'given continuously during' is that matching signal at every observation of the window (holdsFor): an observation with the indicator off and no matching arm signal breaks it. 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' is respected: the signal is judged separately from the turn. 'a vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', except 'Devices moved by human power', 'Electric bicycles', electric personal assistive mobility devices and 'An electric scooter'), claimed whole.

'the last 100 feet traveled' is a window measured in the distance ego travelled behind the onset (a .path window), read through kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace, monotone'; the figure is the law's literal. It selects the window where t5 holds.
'the last 300 feet traveled' is the same .path window with the law's other literal, through kin.path_length; it selects the window where t7 holds.

'changing the course of a vehicle' is a change of its heading to one side from an observed onset: drv.motion.left_turn_from_onset or drv.motion.right_turn_from_onset, each recognizing a continuous turning stretch whose heading change reaches the turn angle. 'prior to' places the window before the observed onset: the observation at which drv.motion.turning_left (or drv.motion.turning_right) last became true before the recognition, as those concepts' act records declare it. 'a vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

assumptions.meaning: The map or the trace declares the territory at the road user's position a business district or a residence district.
The map or the trace declares the territory at the road user's position a business district or a residence district.

residues.why: The duty holds in every weather: no condition of the weather restricts it, so the duty is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is the recognition of a left turn from an observed onset (drv.motion.left_turn_from_onset with p.left_turn_min_angle, p.turn_yaw_tolerance, p.rest_speed_tolerance, p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) or of a right turn from an observed onset (drv.motion.right_turn_from_onset with p.right_turn_min_angle and the same tolerances).
obligation: Event, recognition and history (rule 4d): the event is the change of course; it is recognized at the judged observation; its observed onset is the last observation at which drv.motion.turning_left (for a left turn; drv.motion.turning_right for a right turn, each with p.turn_yaw_tolerance and p.rest_speed_tolerance) became true, the turning state having held at every observation since (a since operator: turning since (rise of turning and W)). W, read at that onset: where asm.business_or_residence_district holds there, at every observation of the window of the literal 100 ft of path travelled by ego behind the onset (holdsFor .path, kin.path_length), ego's turn indicator is left (sig.turn_indicator = left) or its arm signal means left (sig.hand_signal = left); where it does not hold, the same over the window of the literal 300 ft. For a right turn the matching side is right. The window ends at the onset and is the words' own bound; a window that reaches past the start of the recording is unknown (windowTruncated), as is the duty where the assumption is undeclared and the two windows decide differently. Conduct after the onset is not read.

narrowings.why: A change of course is read as a turn whose heading change from its observed onset reaches the turn angle; a lane change or a gentle departure from the course, whose heading change stays below it, is not read, and a road bend followed through that angle in one turning stretch is read as a turn.

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event
an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', carrying DEF-NRS-484A-095 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'); ego's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' is respected: the part of it the duty reads is e6.

'stop' where prohibited is DEF-NRS-484A-260, 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155) and 'standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-250) are halts too, so their union is a halt (drv.motion.at_rest) other than the excepted ones, which the rule carries beside it: a halt behind a road user ahead in ego's lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) that is itself at rest within p.queue_gap (rel.surface_gap), or a halt while a stop indication governs ego's carrier (dev.governs of a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red or a red_arrow, a dev.stop_sign, or a dev.human_direction indicating stop). 'no person shall' is read through the vehicle's halt (observable_reading agency).
'vehicle' admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions), claimed whole.

'the paved or main-traveled part of the highway': the main-traveled part is the roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'), the paved part also a shoulder whose paved attribute holds (st.shoulder, 'paved attribute'); ego's footprint overlaps one (rel.occupies) lying on the highway of e1 (st.on_way).

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap on e13): that a vehicle is disabled so that it cannot avoid stopping is a condition of the vehicle no atom carries; hazard lamps (sig.hazard, 'both indicators flashing together') are a lamp state, and an engine stopped (kin.engine_running) is 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt' nor for a vehicle that cannot move.

operationalizations.convention: Off-road standing place within braking reach: halting off the paved or main-traveled part is practicable where a region off it lies within p.offroad_stop_reach of the halted vehicle's body (drv.position.near_region over st.region_geometry): a shoulder whose paved attribute does not hold (st.shoulder) or a parking space (st.parking_space) that does not overlap the roadway. The distance to the nearest such place enters the bound.

assumptions.meaning: The map or the trace declares the territory at the road user's position a business district or a residence district.

residues.why: Whether the vehicle is attended or unattended does not change the duty: it is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is a vehicle; at the judged observation ego occupies a roadway, or a shoulder whose paved attribute holds, lying on a highway (st.on_way), asm.business_or_residence_district does not hold there, and ego is halted (drv.motion.at_rest with p.rest_speed_tolerance) other than behind a road user ahead in its lane at rest within p.queue_gap or under a stop indication governing its carrier. Exception: a disabled vehicle (gap on e13).
obligation: It is not the case that a region off the paved or main-traveled part (a shoulder whose paved attribute does not hold, or a parking space not overlapping the roadway) lies within p.offroad_stop_reach of ego's body (drv.position.near_region over st.region_geometry).

narrowings.why: 'no person shall' is read through the vehicle's halt, whoever controls it.
Practicability is read only through an off-road standing place within reach; its size and surface are not read.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: Stopping-sight-distance model of highway design (AASHTO Green Book), with the curve side-friction and lane-width relations of the same guides. Surface and weather select the deceleration: p.stopping_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.stopping_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.stopping_decel_dry (Term.cond over drv.motion.stopping_distance calls with p.perception_reaction_time). The stopping distance may not exceed the sight distance of the place (st.sight_distance) nor the visibility distance (env.visibility); for every road user ahead of ego in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), the traffic, the gap (rel.surface_gap) may not fall below the speed times p.perception_reaction_time; the speed squared times the curvature (st.curvature) may not exceed p.curve_lateral_accel; the speed times p.lane_width_speed_time may not exceed the width (st.lane_width) of the lane ego occupies (st.lane, rel.occupies). Each measured magnitude enters its bound. The standard is the whole duty: the rule is a surrogate.

applicability: ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); the duty is judged at every observation.
obligation: At every observation, with D the stopping distance of ego (drv.motion.stopping_distance with p.perception_reaction_time and the deceleration selected by Term.cond: p.stopping_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.stopping_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.stopping_decel_dry): D is at or below st.sight_distance at ego's place and at or below env.visibility; ego's speed (kin.speed) squared times st.curvature at its place is at or below p.curve_lateral_accel; for every lane l ego occupies (rel.occupies), ego's speed times p.lane_width_speed_time is at or below st.lane_width of l; and for every road user u other than ego that is ahead of ego in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), the gap between them (rel.surface_gap) is at or above ego's speed times p.perception_reaction_time. narrowings.why: 'drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

The factors are read only through the contracts named: traffic through the road users ahead in ego's lane (crossing and oncoming traffic, and its density, are not read); surface through wet and icy or snow-covered states; width through the width of the lane ego occupies; weather through precipitation and visibility distance; the catch-all 'other highway conditions' only through curvature and the sight distance of the place (grade, darkness and works are not read).

contract: The heading change of road user a since it entered region r: the signed change of the direction its body points (degrees, left positive), accumulated from the observation at which a's footprint last came to overlap r, where it is zero, to the observation, whether or not a still overlaps r. Measured by integrating a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, deg/s, left positive) from the observation at which a's occupancy of r (rel.occupies) last became true, with the step bound, the largest interval between consecutive observations integrated across. It is unknown where that entry is not observed (a occupied r from the start of the recording, or an unknown occupancy could hide the entry), where an interval between consecutive observations since the observation before the entry exceeds the step bound, or where a yaw rate since the entry is missing. Not a stand-in for a turn: it is a magnitude that a caller bounds, and a road user that follows a bend of the way through r accumulates the bend's heading change.
